operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple ASCII (ID, name, Nationality, meter_100, Stadium_ID, Opening_year); no spaces or mixed-case table names, but column case varies (ID vs name vs Nationality) so case-insensitive column lookup is exercised.
Tiny DB: swimmer=8, stadium=10, event=6, record=13 rows; max_rows_per_table sampling never triggers, original_values are complete.
record has composite PK (Swimmer_ID, Event_ID) and a non-PK 'ID' column that is NOT unique in the DDL sense but is distinct=13 in data; composite-PK member -> max_l0=30 path is exercised.
record.Swimmer_ID and record.Event_ID are FK children of swimmer.ID and event.ID; event.Stadium_ID -> stadium.ID; all parents exist and are unique (PK).
No self-references, no dangling FKs, no NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints, no indexes/views/triggers in DDL.
Declared types: INT/REAL/TEXT only; no date/timestamp/bool/bit/year/char(n) types, so Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers are never selected.
event.Year is TEXT storing 4-digit years ('2016','2011',...) -> dispatches to String fuzzer, not Number/Date; text-stored dates are NOT detected.
swimmer.meter_200..meter_700 and Time are TEXT storing 'M:SS.ss' lap times ('1:57.10','7:47.91') -> String fuzzer; storage class text matches declared TEXT.
swimmer.meter_100 is REAL storing floats (57.31) -> Number fuzzer with scale from REAL (no args -> default scale).
stadium.Opening_year is INT storing 2004..2007 -> Number fuzzer; small distinct (4) so literal pool reuse dominates.
record.Result is TEXT with only 3 distinct values ('NC','Win','Loss') -> String fuzzer with tiny element set; contaminate will produce implausible strings.
No storage-class/declared-type contradictions observed (INT->integer, REAL->real, TEXT->text everywhere).
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on swimmer.ID, stadium.ID, event.ID, record.ID, stadium.Capacity, stadium.Opening_year, event.Stadium_ID, record.Swimmer_ID, record.Event_ID: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] plus +-1/+-2 perturbation; Capacity/Opening_year will get negative and huge values (implausible) -> likely FN on range predicates like Capacity > 60000 or Opening_year BETWEEN 2004 AND 2007.

Number fuzzer on swimmer.meter_100 (REAL): floats in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-0.01/+-0.02 perturbation; real lap times ~55-58 will be replaced by implausible magnitudes -> FN on meter_100 < 58 style predicates.

String fuzzer on swimmer.name, stadium.name, stadium.City, stadium.Country, event.Name: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length 0-20 plus contaminate; real names/cities/countries lost -> FN on equality/IN/LIKE predicates over these columns unless literal pool supplies them.
String fuzzer on event.Year (TEXT): random strings, not 4-digit years -> FN on Year = '2016' / Year BETWEEN '2011' AND '2016' unless pool seeds them; also breaks any implicit numeric comparison.
String fuzzer on swimmer.meter_200..meter_700 and Time (TEXT 'M:SS.ss'): random strings, format lost -> FN on any predicate comparing lap times or ordering by Time.
String fuzzer on record.Result (3 distinct): elements NC/Win/Loss reused with p=0.2 fresh; contaminate may corrupt them -> some FN on Result = 'Win' but ties/duplicates preserved so fewer FP.
FK fill: record.Swimmer_ID drawn from swimmer.ID final values, record.Event_ID from event.ID, event.Stadium_ID from stadium.ID; consistent joins preserved, so join-count queries mostly survive.

Composite PK (Swimmer_ID,Event_ID) on record: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate pairs; with small parent sizes (6-8) many rows collapse -> record row count may be much smaller than chosen size, affecting COUNT(*) predicates.
record.ID is not PK and not unique-declared, so drop_unique_duplicates does not filter it; duplicates possible -> FP risk on COUNT(DISTINCT ID) or ID-based joins if queries assume uniqueness.

Small table sizes (choose_table_sizes: level 0 = 1+30u, x4 per level, cap 2500) mean stadium/swimmer/event get tens of rows, record hundreds; original has 6-13 rows so TS instances are much larger -> COUNT comparisons like '> 5' may flip.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers fire (no such declared types), so TS misses on this DB are dominated by Number implausibility and String format loss, not date-template issues.

Literal pool from train SQL will seed some real values (e.g. 'Win','NC','2016', country names) via loose ancestor mapping; columns with no train literals fall back to pure fuzz -> FN concentrated there.
